title: Andalusian Morocco: Casablanca, Rabat, Tangier, Tetouan, Chefchaouen and Fes in 8 Days
meta_title: Andalusian Morocco 8 Days: Tangier, Chefchaouen, Fes
meta_description: 8-day private tour of north Morocco: Rabat, Tangier and Cap Spartel, Tetouan, blue Chefchaouen, the medina of Fes and the Hassan II Mosque.
tagline: Where Moorish Spain and Morocco meet: blue towns, white medinas and the Strait of Gibraltar
facts: Private air-conditioned car with driver; national guide for groups of 4 or more
March to May, September to November
intro: Northern Morocco is where Arab and Andalusian culture have mixed for centuries, brought by Moors and Jews who left Spain. This private tour runs from Casablanca to the royal capital Rabat, Tangier on the Strait of Gibraltar, the white medina of Tetouan, the blue town of Chefchaouen in the Rif mountains and the medieval medina of Fes, before returning to Casablanca for the great Hassan II Mosque. Drives are 3 to 4 hours, and Fes to Casablanca about 3 hours 30 minutes by motorway.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Dirhams
good_to_know.text: The Moroccan dirham cannot be bought outside Morocco. Change money or use ATMs on arrival, and carry cash for souks, taxis and tips; riads and big shops take cards.

good_to_know.title: Dress and photos
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees, especially in the medinas. Always ask before photographing people; some will ask for a small tip.

good_to_know.title: Medina guides and touts
good_to_know.text: Unofficial 'guides' offer to show you the way or the tanneries. Politely refuse and stay with your licensed guide.

good_to_know.title: Mosques and Ramadan
good_to_know.text: Non-Muslims may enter only the Hassan II Mosque in Casablanca, on guided tours. During Ramadan many cafés close by day; eat discreetly.

dining_intro: Moroccan food has excellent vegetarian dishes: vegetable tagine, seven-vegetable couscous, zaalouk (smoked aubergine), bissara (split pea soup), lentils and fresh bread. We tell every riad and cooking teacher your diet in advance.
dining_avoid: Harira soup and many tagines are made with lamb or chicken stock, and smen (aged butter) is common. Ask for 'bla lham' (without meat) and check the stock.
food_card: Nous sommes végétariens stricts. Pas de viande, poisson, fruits de mer ni œufs. Pas d'oignon, d'ail, de pomme de terre, de carotte ni de légumes racines. Pas de bouillon de viande ou de poisson. Merci.
Ana nabati. Bla lham, bla djaj, bla hout, bla bid. Bla bssal, bla touma. Shukran.
We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
